document.title: OpesInsure Mobile Full APK Audit - Consolidated Findings and Proposed Fixes
document.purpose: Single JSON handoff containing all findings reviewed in this conversation, the problem for each finding, and the proposed fix.
document.implementation_instruction: Do not blindly rebuild working modules. Inspect current implementation first, reuse existing APIs/components/routes, implement the proposed fix only where the finding is still present, and preserve backend authorization as authoritative.
document.audit_method: Static analysis of the compiled Android APK plus workflow/route/component/API/security inspection. Runtime-only behavior is explicitly marked as requiring device validation.

evidence_status_legend.confirmed_from_apk: Observed in the compiled APK/static implementation.
evidence_status_legend.confirmed_strength: Verified existing strength that should be preserved.
evidence_status_legend.confirmed_strength_with_gap: Verified strength with a related incompleteness.
evidence_status_legend.confirmed_gap: Gap confirmed from the available compiled implementation.
evidence_status_legend.missing_feature: No corresponding implementation was identified in the audited mobile build.
evidence_status_legend.not_evidenced_in_apk: Not found during static APK inspection; requires source/runtime/backend verification before claiming absence.
evidence_status_legend.runtime_validation_required: Cannot be truthfully scored from static analysis alone.
evidence_status_legend.backend_not_audited: Server-side control cannot be established from the mobile APK.
evidence_status_legend.security_requirement: Required security boundary/behavior even where current baseline may already partially follow it.
evidence_status_legend.proposed_standard: Cross-cutting implementation standard proposed to close repeated gaps.
evidence_status_legend.audit_conclusion: Overall release-readiness conclusion based on the consolidated findings.
evidence_status_legend.confirmed_gap_or_not_standardized: Feature may exist in places but is not consistently available or standardized.
evidence_status_legend.missing_feature_or_not_standardized: No robust standardized implementation was identified.

findings.problem: The top 'Skip' action routes directly to Sign In, so the label does not match the destination.
findings.evidence: Compiled route behavior sends Skip to /(auth)/sign-in.
findings.impact: Creates navigation ambiguity and can make users feel forced into authentication.
findings.proposed_fix: Rename the control to 'Sign in' or make Skip route to a neutral start/auth-choice screen.
findings.acceptance_criteria: The visible label accurately describes the destination in English and French, and no onboarding control has a misleading destination.

findings.problem: The public onboarding promises comparison and purchase but does not provide a public explore/compare path before registration.
findings.evidence: Get Started leads into account creation/authentication.
findings.impact: Adds friction before a user can understand available insurance options.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a public Explore Insurance path: browse product families, answer preliminary questions, view indicative options, then authenticate only when personal data/submission is required.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A logged-out user can browse and compare indicative products without creating an account; authentication begins only when protected data or binding actions are needed.

findings.problem: The final onboarding state exposes several competing destinations: Get Started, Sign In, Verify Certificate, Partner Join and Skip-related navigation.
findings.evidence: Multiple public CTAs target different audiences on the same acquisition surface.
findings.impact: Weakens primary customer conversion hierarchy.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep one dominant customer CTA, demote certificate verification to a utility action, and separate Partner Access visually from customer onboarding.
findings.acceptance_criteria: One primary CTA is visually dominant; partner and certificate-verification actions are clearly secondary and do not compete equally.

findings.problem: The onboarding has better width/fontScale awareness than many authenticated screens, creating inconsistent responsive behavior across the app.
findings.evidence: Onboarding code reacts to screen width/fontScale while operational pages often use fixed truncation/row behavior.
findings.impact: Users may experience a polished onboarding followed by cramped authenticated screens.
findings.proposed_fix: Move responsive primitives used by onboarding into shared app layout components and apply them across authenticated screens.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Operational screens pass the same small-screen and font-scale matrix as onboarding.

findings.problem: Customer Home list titles are hard-limited to one line and metadata to two lines.
findings.evidence: Compiled UI applies one-line title and two-line metadata limits.
findings.impact: Long policy/claim/quote names and French translations can be truncated and hide critical information.
findings.proposed_fix: Allow adaptive two-line titles and 2-3 line metadata, or split critical values into dedicated fields.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No critical policy, claim, renewal or quote identifier is ellipsized at supported widths/font scales.

findings.problem: Payments, wallet and receipts are not prominent on Home despite dedicated payment/wallet routes existing.
findings.evidence: Routes exist for /wallet, /payments, /payments/[id], receipt and refund, but Home emphasis is elsewhere.
findings.impact: Users may miss payment failures, refunds, receipts or outstanding premium status.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a payment/financial status card or action area to Home, driven by outstanding/failure/refund states.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Customer Home surfaces urgent financial status and links directly to payment detail/receipt when relevant.

findings.problem: Home presents multiple domains but does not sufficiently prioritize urgent exceptions over routine cards.
findings.evidence: The screen includes policies, renewals, quotes, claims, notifications and support content.
findings.impact: Critical actions can be buried below ordinary content.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce a priority action feed for payment failed, policy expiring, claim evidence required, KYC incomplete, issuance exception and similar states.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Urgent actionable items appear above normal summary content and disappear after resolution.

findings.problem: The Home page can become vertically dense because many domains are stacked on one screen.
findings.evidence: Multiple sections are rendered on a single scrollable dashboard.
findings.impact: Increases scan time and cognitive load on smaller devices.
findings.proposed_fix: Use prioritized sections, collapsible/limited previews and 'View all' navigation instead of full-depth lists on Home.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Home remains concise while all detailed records remain reachable.

findings.problem: Agent, Broker and Carrier dashboards can hide their WorkspaceMenu when dashboard.metrics is empty because the navigation menu is wrapped inside a generic StatePanel empty-state branch.
findings.evidence: The homes fetch dashboard.metrics, test metrics.length === 0, and the StatePanel can replace children with 'No activity yet' plus Refresh.
findings.impact: A brand-new partner account can lose access to the very tools needed to create the first activity.
findings.proposed_fix: Move permanent navigation/module menus outside StatePanel. Empty state should apply only to metrics/activity widgets.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A brand-new account with zero metrics still sees every permitted module and can create its first valid transaction.

findings.problem: Dashboard metrics are fetched but not meaningfully rendered as operational KPIs on partner Home screens.
findings.evidence: Metrics are used primarily in state handling while Home behaves as a module launcher.
findings.impact: The dashboard does not function as an operational command center.
findings.proposed_fix: Render KPI cards, urgent work queues, SLA/exception indicators and recent activity from the existing metrics payload.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Partner Home displays actionable KPIs and each KPI drills into the corresponding filtered work queue.

findings.problem: Partner homes are primarily static module launchers and do not elevate urgent work.
findings.evidence: Menus expose many modules at equal visual priority.
findings.impact: Users must manually inspect modules to discover work requiring action.
findings.proposed_fix: Add role-specific work queues: leads due, quotes pending, renewals, unpaid premiums, claim tasks, underwriting referrals, reconciliation exceptions, bordereau discrepancies and SLA breaches.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Home shows urgent counts/tasks before the module directory, with one-tap filtered navigation.

findings.problem: The app has reusable button primitives but more than one button family is used (main Button plus AuthPrimaryButton/AuthSecondaryButton), and many screens bypass them.
findings.evidence: Compiled UI includes shared Button variants plus separate authentication button components and many raw Pressable patterns.
findings.impact: Action hierarchy, sizing, accessibility and disabled/loading behavior are not guaranteed consistently.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one canonical AppButton system with primary, secondary, tertiary, danger and text variants; authentication should consume the same underlying primitive.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Primary actions across all routes use the canonical button primitive unless a documented exception exists.

findings.problem: Many one-off Pressable/icon/pill/action implementations bypass the shared button system.
findings.evidence: Compiled screen code contains custom Pressable patterns outside the universal button layer.
findings.impact: Creates inconsistent hit areas, visual affordance, accessibility labels, pressed states and disabled behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace operational raw Pressable CTAs with AppButton, IconButton, ActionRow, FilterChip or SegmentedControl components.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No transactional CTA is implemented as an unstandardized raw Pressable.

findings.problem: Secondary, tertiary, chip and locally styled controls can visually blend with white/light surfaces.
findings.evidence: These controls often use subtle borders, neutral backgrounds and low-elevation styling on light application backgrounds.
findings.impact: Users can perceive real actions as missing, especially under glare, low vision or compressed rendering.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase contrast and affordance: stronger border/background separation, consistent minimum height, icon/text pairing where useful, and explicit pressed/disabled states.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every actionable control is distinguishable from surrounding surfaces without relying on hover or color nuance.

findings.problem: Filter controls do not have a consistently strong visual system for interactive, selected and active-filter states.
findings.evidence: Filter/chip styles vary and some rely mostly on subtle color changes.
findings.impact: Users may not know a filter is interactive or currently active.
findings.proposed_fix: Create a universal FilterButton + FilterSheet + FilterChip system with active count, active chips, Clear All and Apply.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Filters show a visible active count and selected state that remains understandable in grayscale.

findings.problem: Some chips/status/filter states depend heavily on color differentiation.
findings.evidence: Selected/unselected and status states are often represented with color treatment.
findings.impact: Color-vision-deficient users can miss state changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Pair color with text, icon, border, checkmark or shape change.
findings.acceptance_criteria: All status and selection states remain understandable in grayscale.

findings.problem: The shared component layer already includes useful accessibility roles, labels, busy/disabled states, radio semantics and password visibility labels.
findings.evidence: Compiled shared UI contains accessibilityRole/accessibilityState/accessibilityLabel usage.
findings.impact: This is a strength but coverage is uneven.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve these semantics and move all custom actions into standardized accessible primitives.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Shared controls retain correct TalkBack semantics after refactoring.

findings.problem: Custom Pressable controls do not guarantee consistent accessibility labels, roles, hints or states.
findings.evidence: Many screens bypass shared accessible components.
findings.impact: TalkBack users can encounter unlabeled or context-poor actions.
findings.proposed_fix: Audit every custom interactive element and migrate it to an accessible primitive; require label/role/state at component API level.
findings.acceptance_criteria: TalkBack can identify the purpose and state of every interactive control without visual context.

findings.problem: Accessibility hints are comparatively uncommon.
findings.evidence: Labels exist more often than explanatory hints.
findings.impact: Complex actions may be ambiguous to screen-reader users.
findings.proposed_fix: Add concise accessibilityHint text where the action result is not obvious from its label.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Non-obvious controls announce both purpose and consequence.

findings.problem: No meaningful application-level high-contrast mode or explicit adaptation to Android high-text-contrast settings was found.
findings.evidence: Static inspection did not reveal an app-level high-contrast implementation.
findings.impact: Low-vision users may struggle with subtle borders and tertiary controls.
findings.proposed_fix: Add high-contrast design tokens or ensure the default theme independently meets WCAG AA/AAA targets for critical elements; test Android contrast settings.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Critical text and controls meet contrast requirements under default and high-contrast device settings.

findings.problem: Responsive/fontScale handling is not consistent across operational screens.
findings.evidence: Onboarding explicitly considers fontScale while many lists/tabs use hard line limits.
findings.impact: 150-200% text can truncate labels, actions and record metadata.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce large-text-safe layouts, adaptive wrapping and vertical growth; validate 100%, 130%, 150% and 200%.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No critical action or record identity is lost at 200% font size.

findings.problem: Partner tab labels are constrained to one line.
findings.evidence: Compiled tab styling forces single-line labels.
findings.impact: Long French labels and large fonts can truncate.
findings.proposed_fix: Use shorter localized labels, adaptive tab typography, or accessible icon+label behavior without clipping.
findings.acceptance_criteria: All supported locale labels render without ambiguity at large font settings.

findings.problem: MasterSelectField limits selected-value summary lines, making multi-select states hard to read.
findings.evidence: Compiled component constrains summary text.
findings.impact: Several selected values can become opaque or truncated.
findings.proposed_fix: Use chips, '+N selected', expandable summaries, or adaptive wrapping.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can determine the full selection state without reopening the picker.

findings.problem: The shared Screen ScrollView does not set keyboardShouldPersistTaps.
findings.evidence: Compiled shared screen behavior lacks keyboardShouldPersistTaps.
findings.impact: A first tap on a button/select while the keyboard is open may only dismiss the keyboard instead of executing the action.
findings.proposed_fix: Set keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled' (or justified equivalent) in the shared form screen.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Primary form actions execute on the first intentional tap while the keyboard is open.

findings.problem: No consistent shared keyboardDismissMode was found.
findings.evidence: Shared form containers do not enforce a standard dismissal policy.
findings.impact: Keyboard behavior varies by screen and can obstruct content.
findings.proposed_fix: Set a platform-appropriate global keyboardDismissMode and document exceptions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Scrolling/dismissing the keyboard behaves consistently across forms.

findings.problem: The common KeyboardAvoidingView uses fixed height behavior without a meaningful shared vertical offset.
findings.evidence: Compiled common layout uses height behavior.
findings.impact: Long forms can compress or jump awkwardly when the keyboard appears.
findings.proposed_fix: Use platform-specific keyboard avoidance plus scroll-to-focused-field behavior and safe keyboard offsets.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Focused controls and actions remain visible without severe form compression.

findings.problem: Multiline inputs were found without app-wide textAlignVertical='top'.
findings.evidence: Static inspection found many multiline fields and no consistent top vertical alignment.
findings.impact: Android can vertically center or awkwardly position multiline text.
findings.proposed_fix: Put textAlignVertical='top' in the shared multiline input style.
findings.acceptance_criteria: All multiline fields start text at the top consistently on Android.

findings.problem: Shared PickerField/MasterSelectField bottom sheets do not consistently apply safe-area bottom insets while Android edge-to-edge is enabled.
findings.evidence: Compiled app uses edge-to-edge; shared sheet implementations lack safe bottom inset handling.
findings.impact: Bottom actions can sit too close to or behind gesture/navigation areas.
findings.proposed_fix: Use useSafeAreaInsets() and safe bottom padding in every modal/sheet.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Bottom-sheet controls remain fully visible and tappable on gesture and 3-button navigation devices.

findings.problem: Because many custom Pressables exist, a universal 44-48dp minimum hit target cannot be guaranteed from static review alone.
findings.evidence: Custom controls bypass standard component sizing.
findings.impact: Users with motor/visual impairments may struggle to activate small targets.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce minWidth/minHeight and hitSlop in canonical components; run automated/manual target-size audit.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every interactive target is at least 44-48dp or has equivalent hitSlop.

findings.problem: The app cannot yet be certified as fully usable by a blind user despite having accessibility foundations.
findings.evidence: Static APK review cannot validate TalkBack traversal order, modal focus trapping/restoration or complete spoken flow.
findings.impact: Blind users may hit unlabeled controls, dead ends or focus-order problems.
findings.proposed_fix: Run TalkBack end-to-end tests across authentication, quote, payment, policy, claim and partner workflows; fix traversal/focus issues.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A tester can complete each supported critical journey with TalkBack and without visual reliance.

findings.problem: Multiple operational lists terminate without record-detail navigation.
findings.evidence: Agent policies/renewals, Broker policies/claims/renewals and several Carrier modules lack drill-down.
findings.impact: Users can see records but cannot service or inspect them.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce Dashboard -> List -> Detail -> Action -> Confirmation -> Updated Record -> Timeline for every operational object with a stable ID.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No permitted operational object ends at a non-actionable list unless explicitly designed as read-only.

findings.problem: The app has route/deep-link infrastructure, but all newly completed detail flows must preserve back state and refresh behavior.
findings.evidence: The route surface is large (~155 routes), making consistency important.
findings.impact: Users can return to stale or wrong list state after actions if navigation state is not standardized.
findings.proposed_fix: Make detail routes deep-linkable, preserve filters/list state and refresh affected screens after mutation.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Back returns to the prior filtered list and both list/detail reflect the latest server state.

findings.problem: Explicit access-denied/session-expired routes exist, but role shells should avoid exposing modules the user cannot access.
findings.evidence: Carrier and generic workspaces can show broad module menus independent of fine-grained capabilities.
findings.impact: Users encounter avoidable permission errors and confusing navigation.
findings.proposed_fix: Use backend capabilities to hide/disable inaccessible modules while preserving server-side authorization.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A restricted user sees only permitted modules/actions and direct forbidden routes still fail securely server-side.

findings.problem: No dedicated /agent/claims route was found.
findings.evidence: Broker and Carrier have claim modules while Agent does not.
findings.impact: Agents cannot provide consistent post-sale claim assistance from their workspace.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Agent Claims list/detail scoped to authorized customers/policies; allow assistance, evidence forwarding, status tracking and contact actions but no adjudication.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Agent can initiate/assist/track permitted claims but cannot approve, decline or settle them.

findings.problem: Agent Policies rows are rendered without a proper drill-down/detail flow.
findings.evidence: The list exists but no dedicated Agent Policy Detail route is present.
findings.impact: Agent cannot service a sold policy from the policy register.
findings.proposed_fix: Add role-aware PartnerPolicyDetail with policy, customer, insurer, premium, payment, coverage, documents, certificate, claims, renewal and timeline.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every agent policy row opens a detail page and exposes only backend-permitted actions.

findings.problem: Agent renewal records are read-only and have no end-to-end renewal workflow.
findings.evidence: The current renewal screen shows customer/policy/days/status without action navigation.
findings.impact: Renewal opportunities cannot be progressed inside the app.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement renewal detail through eligibility, repricing/requote, customer confirmation, payment, issuance and new policy.
findings.acceptance_criteria: An agent can take an eligible renewal from due to newly issued policy without dead ends.

findings.problem: Agent Client Detail summarizes customer information and 360 counts but related records are not consistently operational/drillable.
findings.evidence: Current content includes customer data, KYC, origin lock, policy count, next renewal, beneficiaries and timeline.
findings.impact: Agents must leave context or cannot act on related records.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabs/sections for Policies, Quotes/Proposals, Claims, Payments, Documents, KYC, Beneficiaries and Activity with deep links.
findings.acceptance_criteria: All authorized related records can be opened directly from Customer 360.

findings.problem: Agent Sale Detail does not visibly complete the full server-verified payment -> proposal -> issuance -> policy -> commission lifecycle.
findings.evidence: Current sale detail contains product, premium, payment phone/status, commission and payment request.
findings.impact: Agents cannot clearly resolve payment/issuance exceptions or follow sale completion.
findings.proposed_fix: Add payment attempt history, failure reason, retry, verified timestamp, receipt, proposal link, issuance status, policy link, documents and commission-accrual state.
findings.acceptance_criteria: PAYMENT_OK_ISSUANCE_FAILED and similar exception states are visible and actionable without falsely marking a policy issued.

findings.problem: Agent wallet has withdrawal creation/history but lacks a detailed withdrawal lifecycle page.
findings.evidence: Withdrawal entries do not provide a full status/audit drill-down.
findings.impact: Failed or delayed withdrawals are hard to diagnose.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Withdrawal Detail with reference, amount, destination, verification, approval, processing, paid/failed, transaction reference, failure reason and audit history.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every withdrawal can be inspected end-to-end and safely retried/cancelled only when permitted.

findings.problem: A dedicated Agent Staff / Agency Staff role model was not found in the compiled role set.
findings.evidence: Existing roles include Agent/Freelance Agent, Broker roles and Carrier roles.
findings.impact: An agency with multiple employees cannot cleanly separate organization administrator from salesperson permissions.
findings.proposed_fix: If multi-user agencies are in scope, add AGENCY_ADMIN and AGENCY_STAFF (or equivalent) with explicit organization membership and permissions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Agency admins can manage internal staff without granting cross-agent data access to independent agents.

findings.problem: Broker Client Detail shows customer/portfolio data but lacks a first-class New Quote/New Business action path.
findings.evidence: Current detail includes origin lock, policy count, balance, next renewal and Customer 360.
findings.impact: Brokers cannot naturally progress existing clients into new business.
findings.proposed_fix: Add New Quote, Start New Business, View Policies, Claims, Renewals, Receivables, Documents, KYC and Timeline actions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: From an existing customer, permitted broker users can start new business without returning to a generic module list.

findings.problem: Broker lacks clear equivalents of agent new-lead/new-client/new-sale/new-quote entry points.
findings.evidence: Broker routes include leads/clients/quotes but no obvious broker creation routes equivalent to agent creation flows.
findings.impact: The brokerage workspace can become a servicing-only shell instead of a sales workflow.
findings.proposed_fix: Add New Lead, Register/Link Customer, Create Quote and Start Assisted Sale using shared quote infrastructure and broker attribution rules.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker can create a lead/customer/quote and progress it to policy issuance within permitted scope.

findings.problem: Broker Policies is a list with no dedicated broker policy detail.
findings.evidence: No /broker/policies/[id] operational detail route was identified.
findings.impact: Brokers cannot service policies or drill into documents/renewals/claims.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Broker Policy Detail with customer, carrier, policy data, payments, documents, claims, renewal, commission attribution, receivable state and timeline.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every policy row opens a role-aware detail page.

findings.problem: Broker Claims rows are non-drillable.
findings.evidence: List exists without Broker Claim Detail.
findings.impact: Brokers cannot assist customers through claims from the app.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Broker Claim Detail with claim, policy, customer, evidence requirements, info requests, inspection, decision, settlement and timeline; allow assistance but not adjudication.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker can track and assist claims while insurer-only decisions remain unavailable.

findings.problem: Broker Renewals is effectively a read-only pipeline.
findings.evidence: No record-level renewal route/action chain is present.
findings.impact: Renewal work cannot be progressed.
findings.proposed_fix: Add renewal detail with assignment, eligibility, requote, customer decision, payment and issuance.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker can complete a renewal without dead ends.

findings.problem: Broker Production is an OperationsList with no record-detail flow.
findings.evidence: Production records are visible but not operational.
findings.impact: Cannot trace a production item to its customer, policy, producer or commission.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Production Record Detail with policy, customer, carrier, premium, commission, producer, payment, issuance, dates and audit source.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Production rows drill into linked customer/policy/commission records.

findings.problem: Broker Commissions shows statements/accruals and totals but lacks robust accrual and statement detail.
findings.evidence: Current mobile UI is mostly summary/list level.
findings.impact: Commission disputes, reversals, basis and settlement attribution are hard to inspect.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Commission Accrual Detail and Commission Statement Detail with policy/customer/carrier/basis/rate/status/adjustments/settlement/payment references.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every commission and statement row opens complete auditable details.

findings.problem: Broker Receivables lacks robust record-level reconciliation and drill-down.
findings.evidence: Current screen combines statements/accrual information without a full receivable lifecycle.
findings.impact: Outstanding amounts and allocations are difficult to resolve.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Receivable Detail, ageing, allocations, reconciliation history, related customer/carrier and export.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can trace each receivable balance to source transactions and reconciliation events.

findings.problem: Broker Compliance is essentially a list.
findings.evidence: OperationsList renders compliance records without a dedicated detail workflow.
findings.impact: Expiry, evidence and remediation cannot be managed cleanly.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Compliance Record Detail with licence/certificate metadata, issuer, expiry, verification, document, requirements and review history.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Each compliance item exposes status, evidence and permitted remediation actions.

findings.problem: Broker Staff supports list/invite but lacks a robust Staff Member Detail and administration lifecycle.
findings.evidence: Current functionality includes staff, pending invitations, phone invite and one-time code.
findings.impact: Admins cannot fully manage roles, assignments, status and access history from mobile.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Staff Member Detail with role, permissions, assigned work, status, last activity and admin actions for permission change, suspend/reactivate, invitation revoke and work transfer.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker Admin can manage staff lifecycle without exposing admin actions to normal broker staff.

findings.problem: BROKER_STAFF is routed to a generic /workspace/[role] shell whose modules render tabular rows without rich record-level workflows.
findings.evidence: Generic Module renders horizontal table columns/rows; Broker Admin has richer dedicated broker routes.
findings.impact: Broker staff can be trapped in Dashboard -> Module -> Table -> dead end while admins have operational flows.
findings.proposed_fix: Route broker staff into the same broker shell as broker admin and drive module/action visibility with backend permissions/capabilities.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker Staff can perform all assigned operational work through broker-native screens without receiving admin-only actions.

findings.problem: Carrier Quote Request Detail is comparatively deep and should be preserved.
findings.evidence: It includes risk snapshot, SLA, review, premium/tax/fees, pricing, conditions, validity, offer and decline flows.
findings.impact: Rewriting it risks regression.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve and reuse its interaction patterns as a benchmark for weaker modules.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Existing quote-request functionality remains unchanged while weaker modules adopt equivalent depth.

findings.problem: Referral Detail supports decision actions but lacks some enterprise workflow controls.
findings.evidence: Current flow includes approve within authority, request information and decline.
findings.impact: Complex cases need assignment, escalation and condition tracking.
findings.proposed_fix: Add assignment/reassignment, escalation above authority, second approval, underwriting conditions, evidence and complete decision history when backend permits.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Underwriters can escalate/assign without client-side authority assumptions.

findings.problem: Carrier Proposals list has no carrier-specific Proposal Detail.
findings.evidence: Customer proposal screen cannot safely substitute because customer actions differ.
findings.impact: Carrier staff cannot fully review proposal, risk, payment, underwriting and issuance context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Carrier Proposal Detail with proposal, customer, intermediary, risk, disclosures, documents, premium, payment, underwriting, info requests, issuance and policy link.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every proposal row opens a carrier-safe detail page with capability-driven actions.

findings.problem: Carrier Product cards support pause/resume but no full Product Detail page was found.
findings.evidence: Tariff/product metadata is mostly card-level.
findings.impact: High-impact product configuration/history is difficult to inspect.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Product Detail with version, tariff/history, coverages, exclusions, eligibility, risk questions, commission configuration, sales channels, effective dates, regulatory documents and audit log.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Product actions are auditable and product versions are inspectable.

findings.problem: Issuance approval/rejection can be performed from a relatively shallow card/queue without a full issuance record review page.
findings.evidence: Current issuance screen supports approve/reject and carrier reference.
findings.impact: High-consequence policy issuance can occur without enough context visible to the staff member.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Issuance Detail showing proposal, customer, intermediary, payment verification, product, risk, cover dates, premium, documents, approvals, reference and wording/version before decision.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Approve/Reject/Request Correction occur from a complete detail record with confirmation and step-up when configured.

findings.problem: Carrier Policies is a non-drillable list.
findings.evidence: No dedicated carrier policy detail route was identified.
findings.impact: Staff cannot service, audit or manage issued policies from the register.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Carrier Policy Detail with customer, intermediary, payment/issuance, cover, documents, endorsements, service requests, renewals, claims, commission attribution and audit.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every carrier policy opens a complete detail record.

findings.problem: Carrier Claim Detail has good decision actions but the overall claim file is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Existing flow covers acknowledge, request info, proposed decision, approve/partial/decline, amount/reason/rationale, second approval and timeline.
findings.impact: Claims handlers need evidence, inspection, reserves, assignments and settlement context in one file.
findings.proposed_fix: Add tabs for Evidence, Documents, Parties, Inspection, Repair, Media, Coverage Snapshot, Reserves, Fraud/Risk Flags, Assignment, Requests, Settlement and Review history.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Claims staff can work the complete claim file while preserving maker-checker decisions.

findings.problem: Carrier Payments provides totals/list but no proper payment detail.
findings.evidence: Rows are not operational drill-down records.
findings.impact: Finance staff cannot reconcile or investigate individual payment exceptions effectively.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Payment Detail with reference, customer, policy/proposal, amount, method, gateway/provider ref, timestamps, reconciliation, allocation, webhook verification, refund and audit.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every payment row can be investigated and permissioned reconciliation actions are available.

findings.problem: Distribution Partner rows are non-drillable.
findings.evidence: List shows name/type/policy count/premium/agreement/status without a full partner record.
findings.impact: Carrier cannot inspect agreements, authorization, compliance, production and settlement in context.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Partner Detail with identity, licence, agreement, branches/staff, authorized products, production, commission, settlement, compliance, documents and history.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Partner list rows open auditable partner records with capability-driven actions.

findings.problem: Settlement Detail exists but is mostly read-only.
findings.evidence: It displays status, amount, period, dates, bank ref and line items.
findings.impact: Finance users cannot complete review/reconciliation from mobile where intended.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Review, Approve, Reject/Return, Reconcile, Record Payment, Attach Proof, Resolve Discrepancy and Export where backend permits.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Settlement detail supports the configured finance lifecycle with step-up for sensitive actions.

findings.problem: Carrier Bordereaux is a list-only module.
findings.evidence: No bordereau detail/action workflow was identified.
findings.impact: Policy/premium/commission discrepancies cannot be reviewed from mobile.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Bordereau Detail with broker, period, counts, premium/tax/commission/net, line items, validation errors, discrepancies, documents and audit plus Validate/Return/Accept/Reject/Reconcile/Export actions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every bordereau can be reviewed at summary and line-item level.

findings.problem: No equivalent carrier staff management module was identified despite carrier admin/staff roles existing.
findings.evidence: Route inventory lacks a clear /carrier/staff management flow.
findings.impact: Carrier admins cannot manage mobile staff lifecycle from the carrier shell.
findings.proposed_fix: If in mobile scope, add Staff Directory, Invite, Staff Detail, Role/Permissions, Department/Scope, Status, Activity and audit with suspend/reactivate/revoke/transfer actions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Carrier Admin can manage staff membership without exposing those controls to ordinary staff.

findings.problem: Carrier roles enter the same shell and module visibility does not appear consistently capability-filtered at the Home-menu level.
findings.evidence: Carrier Home exposes Products, Proposals, Underwriting, Issuance, Policies, Claims, Payments, Partners, Settlements and Bordereaux broadly.
findings.impact: Restricted staff may see modules that later fail authorization.
findings.proposed_fix: Have backend return allowed modules/actions and filter or disable the mobile menu accordingly; keep server authorization authoritative.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Restricted staff see only allowed modules/actions and cannot bypass authorization through direct routes.

findings.problem: Specialized operational roles are routed to generic workspaces that are too shallow for transactional work.
findings.evidence: Generic workspace modules render tabular data but lack rich details/actions.
findings.impact: Finance, claims and compliance staff can encounter read-only workflows.
findings.proposed_fix: Route specialized roles into shared Carrier Claims/Finance/Compliance shells with backend capability scoping rather than duplicating or using a generic table-only workspace.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Specialized staff can complete their assigned transactions through full detail/action workflows.

findings.problem: Agent/Broker customer lists do not expose a proper insurer/company filter.
findings.evidence: The data model contains carrier/product context but mobile customer filtering is basic.
findings.impact: Partners cannot quickly segment customers by insurer.
findings.proposed_fix: Add server-side carrier_id filter and a searchable insurer selector in the universal FilterSheet.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Agent/Broker can show only customers with policies from a selected insurer within authorization scope.

findings.problem: Customer lists do not expose robust insurance class/product-family/product filters.
findings.evidence: No complete multidimensional customer filter UI was found.
findings.impact: Partners cannot target Motor/Health/Life/etc. portfolios or specific products.
findings.proposed_fix: Add product_family_id and product_id filters with server-side pagination.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can combine insurer + product family + exact product filters.

findings.problem: Customer portfolio filtering is missing important dimensions such as customer type, policy status, renewal window, claim state, payment state and KYC state.
findings.evidence: Current lists/search are basic.
findings.impact: Portfolio servicing requires manual scanning.
findings.proposed_fix: Add filters for customer type, policy status, renewal window, claim state, payment state, KYC, city/region where appropriate and origin/ownership.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can combine multiple dimensions and active filters are visible as chips.

findings.problem: Broker Admin cannot filter customers/production/commissions by selling staff member/producer in a standardized way.
findings.evidence: No universal producer filter is exposed across the relevant screens.
findings.impact: Managers cannot analyze or service portfolios by producer.
findings.proposed_fix: Add producer_user_id, branch_id and team filters to backend/mobile where permitted.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker Admin can filter customers and commission records by staff member/producer.

findings.problem: Portfolio search is not designed as a universal cross-identifier search.
findings.evidence: Current search is basic and does not consistently span policy/quote/claim/vehicle/business identifiers.
findings.impact: Users need multiple screens to locate a known customer-related record.
findings.proposed_fix: Support authorized search across customer name, phone, email, customer ref, policy, quote, claim, vehicle registration and business registration.
findings.acceptance_criteria: One portfolio search returns authorized matches with clear entity type.

findings.problem: No robust saved/recent filter workflow was identified.
findings.evidence: Filters are not standardized across modules.
findings.impact: High-frequency operational searches must be rebuilt repeatedly.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Save Filter and Recent Filters to the universal filter framework.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can reapply a saved filter and the saved query remains permission-safe.

findings.problem: Commission screens do not expose a proper insurer/carrier filter.
findings.evidence: Accrual/statement data exists, but multidimensional filtering is absent.
findings.impact: Partners cannot reconcile earnings by insurance company.
findings.proposed_fix: Add carrier_id filter to commission ledger and backend query.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Commission ledger can be filtered by insurer with accurate totals.

findings.problem: Commission screens do not expose product-family or exact-product filters.
findings.evidence: No comprehensive commission filter sheet was found.
findings.impact: Partners cannot analyze Motor/Health/Life/product profitability.
findings.proposed_fix: Add product_family_id and product_id filters and filtered KPI aggregation.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Commission totals and rows update correctly for selected product dimensions.

findings.problem: Broker Admin cannot filter commission by the agent/staff member who sold the policy.
findings.evidence: Producer dimension is not exposed as a standard commission filter.
findings.impact: Brokerage cannot manage producer performance or reconcile staff-attributed earnings.
findings.proposed_fix: Add producer_user_id/branch/team filters with permission scope.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Broker Admin can filter commission by producer without exposing other organizations' data.

findings.problem: Commission screens do not expose a complete paid/unpaid/lifecycle filter system.
findings.evidence: Existing totals include concepts such as pending/available/paid, but the operational ledger is not fully filterable.
findings.impact: Users cannot quickly isolate unpaid, reversed, adjusted or disputed earnings.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement lifecycle states: Estimated, Pending Eligibility, Accrued, Available, Statement, Approved for Payout, Paid, Reversed, Adjusted, Disputed, Withheld; include All/Unpaid/Paid shortcuts.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Ledger and KPI totals correctly reflect selected lifecycle states.

findings.problem: Commission UI lacks standardized sale/issue/accrual/payment date filtering.
findings.evidence: No universal date filter workflow is present.
findings.impact: Period reconciliation is cumbersome.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Today/Week/Month/Previous Month/Quarter/Year/Custom and a selectable date basis: sale, policy issue, accrual or payment.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can reproduce a statement period using date filters.

findings.problem: Commission summary numbers are not consistently tied to drill-down filtered ledgers.
findings.evidence: Current mobile experience is summary/list oriented.
findings.impact: Users cannot explain totals quickly.
findings.proposed_fix: Make KPI cards clickable and open the ledger with the exact underlying filter.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every KPI/chart has a deterministic drill-down to source rows.

findings.problem: Commission accrual/statement records lack complete record-level detail in mobile.
findings.evidence: Current screens emphasize totals and lists.
findings.impact: Users cannot verify basis, rate, policy attribution, reversals and settlement.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Commission Detail with policy, customer, insurer, product, producer, premium, basis, rate, amount, eligibility, issuance/payment state, statement, settlement, adjustments and audit.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every commission row is auditable to policy and payment.

findings.problem: An independent Agent must not gain cross-agent commission visibility merely because producer filtering is added.
findings.evidence: Current role model treats Agent as an individual role.
findings.impact: Poor scoping could expose commercially sensitive commission data.
findings.proposed_fix: Scope Agent commission endpoints to authorized own/organization portfolio. Use separate agency roles for multi-staff organizations.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Independent agents cannot query unrelated agents' commissions even by crafted API parameters.

findings.problem: Agent and Broker roles do not have unrestricted approve/issue-policy actions; this is the correct safe baseline.
findings.evidence: Issuance actions exist in Carrier workspace.
findings.impact: Granting blanket issuance to intermediaries would weaken insurer authority and auditability.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep insurer-owned issuance by default. Agents/brokers may prepare/submit/track business and view issued documents.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No intermediary can issue a policy unless backend explicitly grants delegated authority.

findings.problem: There is no explicit mobile model for limited delegated underwriting/issuance authority from an insurer to an intermediary.
findings.evidence: Current baseline separates intermediary and carrier issuance.
findings.impact: A future blanket role override would be unsafe.
findings.proposed_fix: Create delegated_authority with carrier, partner, products, territory, limits, risk classes, effective/expiry dates, actions, second-approval thresholds and agreement reference.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Delegated issuance is possible only within server-validated scope and every use is audited.

findings.problem: Issuance should not always be a universal one-click approval.
findings.evidence: Current carrier issuance supports approve/reject; other flows already show second-approval concepts.
findings.impact: High-value or exceptional policies need separation of duties.
findings.proposed_fix: Support configurable Underwriter Review -> Issuance Verification -> Second Approval -> Issue, with straight-through only for allowed cases.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Threshold/authority rules are server enforced and decision history records reviewer/approver/issuer.

findings.problem: The app already includes signed-in device/session management with current-device identification, last-seen/platform data, per-device revocation and sign-out-everywhere.
findings.evidence: Account devices route and session controls are present.
findings.impact: This is a useful security control that should be preserved and made consistently reachable by all roles.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the feature and expose it consistently in Account > Security for customer, agent, broker, carrier and specialized staff roles.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every authenticated role can view/revoke its own sessions.

findings.problem: The app lacks a full login/logout/security-event history.
findings.evidence: Device list shows active sessions but not a complete audit of authentication events.
findings.impact: Users cannot verify when/where account access occurred or investigate suspicious events.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Account > Security > Login Activity with successful/failed sign-ins, OTP/password/biometric events, password changes, new devices, revocations, logout, session expiry, step-up and attestation failures.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can review chronological security activity with date/time, device, app version, masked IP, approximate server-derived location, method, outcome and risk state.

findings.problem: Signed-in device entries do not provide a rich device detail/audit view.
findings.evidence: Current feature is primarily list/revoke.
findings.impact: Users have limited context before revoking a session.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Device Detail with model/name, OS, app version, first/last seen, current session, trust/attestation status, last auth and approximate network location.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can inspect and revoke a device from a dedicated detail screen.

findings.problem: No comprehensive user-facing alert workflow for high-risk account events was established from the APK.
findings.evidence: Session controls exist, but full event alerting was not found.
findings.impact: Compromised-account response may be delayed.
findings.proposed_fix: Send notification/email/SMS per preferences for new device, password/identity changes, sign-out-everywhere, repeated failures, integrity failure and payout-destination changes; include Secure Account action.
findings.acceptance_criteria: High-risk events trigger actionable alerts and security-center navigation.

findings.problem: Broker/Carrier admins need organization-level staff security status without exposing unnecessary personal device data.
findings.evidence: Current personal device management does not equal staff account administration.
findings.impact: Admins cannot quickly identify dormant/compromised staff accounts.
findings.proposed_fix: In Staff Detail expose account status, last successful sign-in, active-session count and security status; allow suspend organization access and force reauthentication under permission.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Admins can secure staff access while detailed device/IP data remains restricted by privacy/security permissions.

findings.problem: The APK uses Hermes, React Native New Architecture and packaged baseline profiles.
findings.evidence: Static APK inspection identified these production-oriented performance features.
findings.impact: These are strong foundations.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve them and measure runtime regressions on low-end devices.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Release builds retain Hermes/New Architecture/baseline profile behavior.

findings.problem: The audited APK is 97,032,612 bytes (~92.5 MiB) and is a universal build containing multiple ABIs.
findings.evidence: Static APK inspection found arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64 payloads.
findings.impact: Large direct-download size increases installation friction and data cost.
findings.proposed_fix: Prefer Android App Bundle/ABI splits for Play distribution; remove unnecessary native assets/ABIs/fonts for direct APK builds.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Typical user download size is materially reduced while required device architectures remain supported.

findings.problem: A large Inter font asset set is packaged.
findings.evidence: Static APK review found many Inter font files.
findings.impact: Adds package weight and memory/resource overhead.
findings.proposed_fix: Subset to actually used weights/styles or use variable-font strategy if compatible.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Unused font files are removed without visual regression.

findings.problem: A mainstream crash/ANR/performance monitoring SDK was not clearly evidenced in the APK.
findings.evidence: Static inspection did not reveal an obvious Sentry/Bugsnag/Datadog-style integration.
findings.impact: Startup regressions, ANRs and dropped frames can reach production without rapid diagnosis.
findings.proposed_fix: Add or verify production monitoring for crash-free sessions, ANR, startup time, API latency, release version and slow-screen traces.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Operations can correlate crashes/performance regressions to app version and route.

findings.problem: Actual 60/90/120 Hz smoothness and dropped-frame rate cannot be determined from static APK inspection.
findings.evidence: Runtime profiling is required.
findings.impact: Animation/list jank may remain undiscovered.
findings.proposed_fix: Profile cold/warm startup, navigation, long lists, sheets and forms on low-end and high-refresh Android devices.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Critical flows meet agreed frame-time and dropped-frame budgets on target hardware.

findings.problem: The 155-route app and ~4 MB Hermes bundle need explicit low-memory device testing.
findings.evidence: Architecture is substantial and APK is large.
findings.impact: 2-3 GB RAM devices common in target markets may expose startup/memory issues.
findings.proposed_fix: Benchmark on representative low-end Cortex-A53/A55 class hardware, weak networks and low storage.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Startup, memory and navigation remain within defined budgets on minimum-supported hardware.

findings.problem: Refresh/focus/sync behavior is not standardized across every operational screen.
findings.evidence: Customer Home has pull-to-refresh and sync/network machinery exists, but no universal freshness contract was found.
findings.impact: Users may act on stale operational data without realizing it.
findings.proposed_fix: Standardize lastUpdatedAt, pull-to-refresh, focus revalidation, stale indicator, offline/sync state and mutation invalidation.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every operational screen exposes consistent freshness semantics.

findings.problem: High-priority work queues do not have an app-wide real-time/freshness policy.
findings.evidence: Dashboards are largely module launchers.
findings.impact: Underwriting, claim, payment or renewal tasks can remain stale.
findings.proposed_fix: Define polling/push/focus-refresh strategy per domain based on SLA sensitivity.
findings.acceptance_criteria: High-priority queues update within the defined service freshness target without excessive network/battery use.

findings.problem: The APK has a relatively mature domain/API structure covering payments, policies, claims, proposals, quotes, roles, support, security, finance and offline synchronization.
findings.evidence: Static compiled code exposes centralized API/domain layers.
findings.impact: This foundation should be retained.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not rewrite the architecture; complete missing UI workflows on top of existing services.
findings.acceptance_criteria: New screens reuse existing domain services instead of duplicating API logic.

findings.problem: Backend/API capability is deeper than several mobile workflows.
findings.evidence: Rich service APIs coexist with list-only mobile modules.
findings.impact: Users encounter artificial mobile limitations despite backend capability.
findings.proposed_fix: Complete role-aware detail/action screens before adding new domain breadth.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every exposed list has the detail/action depth supported by backend permissions.

findings.problem: Screens can bypass shared UI primitives and invent actions/filters independently.
findings.evidence: Raw Pressable/custom patterns coexist with shared components.
findings.impact: Causes inconsistent styling, accessibility and behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce shared primitives at lint/review level; prohibit custom transactional buttons/filters without explicit exception.
findings.acceptance_criteria: New/modified screens pass a design-system conformance check.

findings.problem: Generic table-based workspaces are used for operational roles that need rich domain workflows.
findings.evidence: BROKER_STAFF and specialized carrier roles are routed to generic workspace modules.
findings.impact: The same organization gets two UX models and staff receive shallow functionality.
findings.proposed_fix: Use shared domain shells plus backend capabilities instead of a generic read-only workspace for transactional roles.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Operational staff can complete assigned domain workflows using the same core screens as admins, with restricted actions.

findings.problem: Role names are used heavily, but fine-grained capability-driven rendering is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Carrier menu breadth and generic workspace behavior indicate role-shell coupling.
findings.impact: Role proliferation and overexposure of unavailable actions become likely.
findings.proposed_fix: Have backend return permissions/capabilities/allowed_actions per module/record and render UI from those.
findings.acceptance_criteria: UI never grants authority merely because of a role string, and server still enforces every action.

findings.problem: Detail pages do not follow one consistent loading/error/offline/audit/action contract.
findings.evidence: Operational depth varies widely between modules.
findings.impact: Users experience inconsistent states and error recovery.
findings.proposed_fix: Standardize detail header, statuses, overview, documents, related records, activity/audit, loading/404/403/offline/stale/error/retry and capability actions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every new detail route conforms to the shared contract and design tokens.

findings.problem: Production API uses HTTPS.
findings.evidence: Audited production API base is HTTPS.
findings.impact: Provides transport encryption baseline.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve strict TLS and modern server configuration.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No production endpoint falls back to cleartext HTTP.

findings.problem: Secure local token/secret storage infrastructure is present.
findings.evidence: Static APK inspection identified SecureStore-style encrypted/device storage logic.
findings.impact: Reduces casual token exposure.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep secrets out of AsyncStorage/plain files and validate backup/device-transfer behavior.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Authentication secrets remain in approved secure storage only.

findings.problem: Biometric/local authentication integration is present.
findings.evidence: Android biometric/fingerprint permissions and local auth code exist.
findings.impact: Improves reauthentication UX.
findings.proposed_fix: Use biometrics for local unlock/step-up convenience, not as the sole server authorization mechanism.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Sensitive server actions still require valid authenticated/step-up grants.

findings.problem: Session idle locking and step-up authentication patterns exist.
findings.evidence: The app handles session timeout/relock and X-Step-Up-Grant style sensitive-action authorization.
findings.impact: Strong foundation for high-risk actions.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend step-up consistently to issuance, payout, sensitive profile/security and finance actions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Configured high-risk actions cannot complete without valid step-up.

findings.problem: Idempotency keys are generated for relevant requests.
findings.evidence: Network layer includes Idempotency-Key handling.
findings.impact: Reduces duplicate financial transactions on retry.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve and extend idempotency to all payment/issuance/settlement mutations where required.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Retries cannot create duplicate monetary or policy-binding operations.

findings.problem: The app includes secure-screen configuration intended to prevent screenshots/screen recording of protected content.
findings.evidence: Custom security plugin configuration enables FLAG_SECURE behavior.
findings.impact: Helps reduce casual screen capture of sensitive data.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply selectively where required and verify UX for receipts/documents that legitimately need sharing.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Sensitive screens are protected while approved document-sharing flows remain usable.

findings.problem: Device-attestation API contracts exist but native Google Play Integrity / App Attest evidence was not evidenced as fully wired into this APK.
findings.evidence: The app references device-attestation nonce/assessment and correctly notes that JS alone cannot prove device integrity.
findings.impact: Rooted/repacked/emulated/high-risk devices may lack strong server-verifiable trust signals.
findings.proposed_fix: Implement Google Play Integrity on Android and App Attest/DeviceCheck on iOS, verify server-side and feed results into risk decisions.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Sensitive sessions/actions carry server-verified attestation results and degraded devices follow a documented risk policy.

findings.problem: Dedicated root/jailbreak/tamper signals were not clearly evidenced.
findings.evidence: Static inspection did not show a convincing dedicated implementation.
findings.impact: Compromised-device risk may be underrepresented.
findings.proposed_fix: Add layered risk signals (not sole hard-block): integrity verdict, debug/hook indicators, package/signature checks, emulator/risk signals and server-side anomaly scoring.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Compromised signals influence risk/step-up while false positives do not automatically lock legitimate users without recovery.

findings.problem: OkHttp pinning capability exists in dependencies but application-specific certificate pins were not evidenced.
findings.evidence: No clear OpesInsure pin configuration was found.
findings.impact: TLS remains standard-secure, but high-risk threat models may want MITM hardening.
findings.proposed_fix: Make an explicit pinning decision; if used, implement backup pins and rotation strategy to avoid outages.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Security documentation records whether pinning is used and operational rotation is tested.

findings.problem: Expo Updates is configured, but explicit custom OTA update code-signing configuration was not clearly evidenced during this audit.
findings.evidence: Static inspection showed Expo Updates production configuration but not a definitive signing setup.
findings.impact: A weak OTA trust chain could affect a large part of the JS application.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify and enforce Expo update signing, channel/environment separation and rollback controls.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Production OTA updates are cryptographically verified and cannot be accepted from an unauthorized channel.

findings.problem: The APK uses modern Android signing (v2 identified).
findings.evidence: Static APK inspection identified v2 signing.
findings.impact: Provides modern package integrity baseline.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve modern signing and protect release keystore/process.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Release pipeline uses protected signing credentials and reproducible signing controls.

findings.problem: The client includes device IDs, secure storage, biometrics, step-up, idempotency, sessions, attestation endpoints and support/fraud-report concepts, but device integrity is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Multiple client fraud/security primitives are present.
findings.impact: Good baseline but not sufficient against compromised devices or server-side fraud patterns.
findings.proposed_fix: Finish native attestation and ensure server-side risk engine consumes device/session/transaction signals.
findings.acceptance_criteria: High-risk actions are scored using server-verified device and behavioral context.

findings.problem: Velocity rules, duplicate identity, synthetic identity, claim duplication, collusion, sanctions/PEP and anomaly models cannot be verified from the mobile APK.
findings.evidence: These controls are server-side by nature and were outside APK evidence.
findings.impact: Production-readiness cannot assume these controls exist.
findings.proposed_fix: Audit backend fraud controls separately and map mobile signals into them.
findings.acceptance_criteria: A separate backend fraud-control audit documents implemented rules, monitoring and escalation.

findings.problem: Mobile must never infer payment success or policy issuance solely from client-side actions.
findings.evidence: Existing design already references server verification and issuance exception states.
findings.impact: Client-side trust could enable false-paid/false-issued presentation.
findings.proposed_fix: All paid/issued states must come from server-verified gateway and carrier state; handle delayed issuance explicitly.
findings.acceptance_criteria: No client-only event can mark a financial transaction paid or a policy issued.

findings.problem: The app has secure offline queue, retry/backoff, migration and sync/network-state infrastructure.
findings.evidence: Static code exposes offline queue and synchronization services.
findings.impact: Strong fit for variable connectivity.
findings.proposed_fix: Preserve and extend domain coverage carefully.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Queued mutations remain durable, scoped and idempotent across restart/connectivity changes.

findings.problem: Offline/sync states are not guaranteed to be presented uniformly across modules.
findings.evidence: Underlying queue/sync architecture is stronger than the visible workflow consistency.
findings.impact: Users may not know whether work is local, pending, synced, conflicted or failed.
findings.proposed_fix: Create universal statuses: Saved locally, Waiting to sync, Syncing, Synced, Conflict, Failed - action needed.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Every offline-capable mutation visibly communicates its current synchronization state.

findings.problem: The app has a real design system, but implementation consistency varies substantially by screen.
findings.evidence: Shared colors/spacing/radius/typography/cards/buttons/chips coexist with custom implementations.
findings.impact: One screen can feel polished while the next feels unfinished or cramped.
findings.proposed_fix: Enforce design tokens and shared primitives; add visual regression tests for critical components/routes.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Critical routes use the same spacing, typography, action hierarchy and state components.

findings.problem: One-line/two-line caps, single-line tabs and constrained summaries create cramping risks on small screens and French localization.
findings.evidence: Multiple compiled components use strict line limits.
findings.impact: Text is truncated rather than layouts adapting.
findings.proposed_fix: Prefer adaptive wrapping, vertical growth and dedicated metadata rows over ellipsis for critical data.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Critical content remains readable on smallest supported width, French locale and 200% font scale.

findings.problem: Production crash/ANR observability is not clearly established from the APK.
findings.evidence: No obvious mainstream monitoring integration was evidenced.
findings.impact: Production blockers can remain invisible or difficult to correlate.
findings.proposed_fix: Add/verify crash, ANR and performance telemetry with release/version/user-safe identifiers.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Operations can identify top crashes/ANRs by app version and route within the agreed response window.

findings.problem: The app has strong foundations but still contains P0 workflow, accessibility, security and navigation blockers.
findings.evidence: Confirmed issues include empty-dashboard trap, dead-end detail flows, weak action visibility, incomplete device attestation and incomplete role workflows.
findings.impact: Shipping as final unrestricted production could block legitimate users or weaken trust/security.
findings.proposed_fix: Do not declare final production readiness until all P0 items and agreed P1 security/accessibility items pass acceptance tests.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Release checklist shows zero unresolved P0 issues and signed-off accessibility/security/role-workflow tests.

findings.problem: A proper Individual/Business/Group customer-type filter is not exposed as a standard portfolio filter.
findings.evidence: Current customer filtering is basic.
findings.impact: Partners cannot segment B2C/B2B portfolios efficiently.
findings.proposed_fix: Add customer_type filter backed by server master data/schema.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Portfolio can be filtered by supported customer entity type.

findings.problem: Customer-origin/ownership visibility is not presented as a standardized filter despite origin-lock concepts existing.
findings.evidence: Client details include origin-lock information.
findings.impact: Partners need to distinguish own-originated, assigned and organization-owned customers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add authorized origin/ownership filters without weakening origin-lock rules.
findings.acceptance_criteria: Users can filter only scopes they are permitted to view; origin lock remains server enforced.

implementation_guardrails: Preserve existing strong flows: Agent/Broker Lead workflows, shared Partner Quote workflow, Carrier Quote Requests, Carrier Underwriting Referral decisions, Carrier Claim decision/maker-checker logic, secure offline queue, step-up authentication, idempotency and origin-lock protections.

No mobile filter, hidden button or role label may be treated as an authorization boundary. Server-side tenant/organization/role/ownership/permission/capability/delegated-authority checks remain mandatory.
Financial and policy-binding state must be server verified. Never mark payment successful or policy issued only from client-side events.
Use one reusable filter framework and one reusable action/button component family.
Use shared role-aware detail pages where domain records are the same; vary actions from backend capabilities rather than duplicating near-identical screens.
Every operational detail page must handle loading, empty/missing, 403, 404, offline, stale, sync-pending, API-error and retry states.
Every mutation must update/refetch the affected detail/list/dashboard state and preserve navigation context.
All new controls must be TalkBack-labelled, large-text safe, non-color-dependent and at least 44-48dp tappable.
Do not expose exact login GPS as a default security-log field; prefer server-derived approximate network location where appropriate.
Do not expose unrelated agents' commissions or customers through new filtering capabilities.
